app.title: FFFBPINN Architecture vs Existing Architecture Demo
app.summary: A person ticks one or more pairs of preset training runs and neural network architectures in a sidebar. The dashboard then draws each chosen model's predicted space-time solution next to a reference solution, along with maps of absolute error. A time slider takes a one-dimensional slice of every solution and error at a chosen instant. Bar charts of relative error and a table of error, runtime and percent change against a baseline run let the person judge which architecture gives the best accuracy for its cost.

task.text: Compare several neural network solvers against a reference solution of a space-time equation, by error fields, error norms and runtime against a baseline.

data.text: Precomputed solution fields on a grid of space and time, one per architecture and training run, with a reference solution, relative error metrics and runtimes stored in preset archive files.
data.item: one architecture's predicted solution field over space and time for one preset run

stage.text: comparing trained model architectures against a reference solution after training, before writing up

mechanism.text: A sidebar checklist of run-and-architecture combinations and a time slider drive every view at once: contour small multiples of solutions and absolute errors, a cross-section line chart at the chosen time, log-scale bar charts of error norms and a markdown table of metrics relative to a baseline, each shown in its own tab.

field.text: physics-informed neural networks with domain decomposition for solving differential equations in computational fluid dynamics

workflow.name: compare model outputs against a reference and weigh error against cost

steps.here: Preset .npz archives are read from a presets folder at startup, and each one becomes a run name crossed with four architectures (PINN, FFPINN, FBPINN, FFFBPINN).
A checkbox group picks any number of run-and-architecture combinations. Every change redraws all the views.
Contour plots of each prediction are tiled two per row beside the reference, on a shared colour scale. Absolute error maps with 100 contour levels are tiled the same way.

steps.step: restrict to one moment and compare there
steps.here: A time slider picks the nearest time row. One chart overlays the reference and every prediction along x, and the other shows each prediction's absolute error along x.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: Relative L2 and L∞ errors are shown as log-scale bars. A table adds runtime, the percent improvement in L2 and the percent slowdown against a 10k PINN baseline, or against the first selection if no such run is chosen.

distinctive: Each prediction is judged against a known reference solution, with the colour scale fixed to the reference's range so the fields are comparable.
Accuracy is weighed against cost: runtime is reported as percent faster or slower than a baseline run, next to the percent change in error.
Both a global error norm (L2) and a worst-case error norm (L∞) are shown on a log scale, because the errors span orders of magnitude.
A time slice turns the 2D space-time fields into 1D profiles, where sharp fronts in the solution show clearly.

parts.title: Architecture Selection
parts.summary: Lets the person tick which preset run and architecture combinations to compare and choose the time for the cross-section, which redraws every view.

parts.title: Comparison tabs
parts.summary: Holds the solution, error, cross-section, metrics, statistics and methodology views in tabs, so the person can switch between them.

parts.title: Solution Heatmaps
parts.summary: Draws the reference and each selected prediction as contour plots over space and time on a shared colour scale, tiled two per row.

parts.title: Error Heatmaps
parts.summary: Shows where each prediction departs from the reference as a fine-grained contour map of absolute error over space and time.

parts.title: 1D Cross-Sections
parts.summary: Overlays the reference and every prediction along space at the slider's time, with a second chart of each prediction's absolute error there.

parts.title: Error Metrics
parts.summary: Compares relative L2 and L∞ errors across the selected combinations as log-scale bar charts.

parts.title: Comparative Analytics
parts.summary: Lists each combination's errors and runtime, with its percent improvement in error and its percent slowdown or speedup against a baseline run.
